question: What type of engine is fitted to the DA 42 NG?

options.text: A liquid-cooled, four-cylinder, four-stroke inline diesel engine with common rail direct injection
An air-cooled, six-cylinder, horizontally opposed AVGAS engine
A liquid-cooled, six-cylinder, two-stroke inline engine
An air-cooled, four-cylinder rotary diesel engine

explanation: AFM 7.9.1 describes the Austro Engine E4-C as liquid-cooled, four-cylinder, four-stroke, inline, with common rail direct injection, wet sump lubrication and a turbocharger with intercooler.

question: What is the propeller speed reducing gear ratio?
explanation: AFM 7.9.1 gives the propeller speed reducing gear ratio as 1:1.69.

question: What is the maximum power output of each engine, and at what RPM/conditions?

options.text: 123.5 kW at 2500 RPM, sea level, ISA
135 kW at 2300 RPM, sea level, ISA
123.5 kW (165.6 DIN-HP) at 2300 RPM, sea level, ISA
114 kW (152.3 DIN-HP) at 2300 RPM, sea level, ISA

explanation: AFM 7.9.1 gives maximum power as 123.5 kW (165.6 DIN-HP) at 2300 RPM at sea level and ISA; maximum continuous power is 113.6 kW (152.3 DIN-HP).

question: Where does each engine's ECU receive its electrical power from when both engines are at standstill?

options.text: The ECU backup battery only
External power only
It has no power source with both engines stopped
The battery

explanation: AFM 7.9.1: each ECU is normally powered by its engine's own generator when running, or by the battery when both engines are at standstill.

question: What must be switched ON before an engine can be cranked at all?

options.text: The ENGINE MASTER switch for that engine
The AVIONIC MASTER switch
The ALTERNATOR switch only
The VOTER switch

explanation: AFM 7.9.1/7.9.3: each engine can only be operated (cranked and run) with its own ENGINE MASTER switch ON.

question: What effect does moving the POWER lever forward to MAX have?

options.text: It engages the ECU TEST sequence
It sets full power (LOAD %)
It sets idle
It only adjusts propeller pitch, not power

explanation: AFM 7.9.3: each power lever sets the desired engine power LOAD (%); forward is MAX, rearward is IDLE.

question: Following a propeller governor failure, what maximum RPM should every effort be made not to exceed?

options.text: 1975 RPM
2250 RPM
2300 RPM
2500 RPM

explanation: AFM 7.9.3 cautions that, following a governor failure, RPM should be adjusted with the power lever and every effort made not to exceed 2300 RPM.

question: What happens automatically if oil pressure to the propeller governor is lost?

options.text: The propeller locks at the current pitch
RPM increases uncontrollably toward overspeed
The affected ECU switches to manual mode
The propeller blades feather

explanation: AFM 7.9.3: a loss of governor oil pressure leads to feathering of the propeller blades, allowing the flight to continue per 3.12.3.

question: Turning the START key switch to the LEFT does what?

options.text: Starts the LH engine
Starts the RH engine
Starts both engines simultaneously
Tests both ECUs

explanation: AFM 7.9.3: turning the START key left starts the LH engine, and right starts the RH engine.

question: For normal operation, what position should both VOTER switches be set to?

options.text: OFF
AUTO
ECU A
ECU B

explanation: AFM 7.9.3: for normal operation both VOTER switches are set to AUTO, letting each engine's ECU A or B control it automatically.

question: At what power lever position and RPM must the ECU TEST procedure be initiated?

options.text: Power lever at IDLE, RPM below 1000 exactly
Power lever at 50%, RPM below 1500
Power lever at IDLE, RPM below approximately 900
Power lever at MAX, RPM at 2300

explanation: AFM 7.9.3: the ECU self-test can only be started with the power lever at IDLE and RPM below approximately 900, and only on the ground.

question: What is the purpose of the ALTERNATE AIR lever?

options.text: It supplies backup electrical power to the ECUs
It opens a bypass around the turbocharger
It controls cabin heat independently of engine bleed air
It draws air from the engine compartment for both engines simultaneously, in case of icing or air filter blockage

explanation: AFM 7.9.3: the single ALTERNATE AIR lever serves both engines simultaneously, providing an alternate air source in case of icing or a blocked filter.

question: How is coolant temperature kept low during engine warm-up, before the radiator is activated?

options.text: A bypass around the radiator is in operation while coolant temperature is low
The intercooler routes air across the coolant expansion tank
The gearbox oil cooler pre-cools the coolant
There is no warm-up bypass; the radiator is always active

explanation: AFM 7.9.6: a bypass around the radiator operates at low coolant temperatures to allow quick engine warm-up; a thermostatic valve activates the radiator once the coolant reaches about 88 °C.

question: At approximately what coolant temperature does the thermostat valve activate the radiator?

options.text: Approximately 120 °C (248 °F)
Approximately 88 °C (190 °F)
Approximately 105 °C (221 °F)
Approximately 60 °C (140 °F)

explanation: AFM 7.9.6 states the radiator is activated by a thermostat valve at approximately 88 °C (190 °F).

question: How many separate oil systems does each engine have?

options.text: Three — engine, gearbox, and turbocharger
One system for lubrication, shared between both engines
Two — one for engine lubrication, one for the gearbox and propeller governor
One shared oil system for everything

explanation: AFM 7.9.7: each engine has two separate oil circuits — engine/turbocharger lubrication, and a second circuit lubricating the gearbox and serving the propeller governor.

question: How is engine oil quantity checked during the pre-flight inspection?

options.text: Only via the G1000 MFD oil quantity page
With a sight glass on the exterior of the cowling
There is no way to check oil quantity before flight
With a dip-stick, through an inspection hole in the upper cowling

explanation: AFM 7.9.7 (and 4A.6.1) describe checking engine oil with a dip-stick through an inspection hole in the upper cowling; gearbox oil is checked visually through a separate inspection hole.

question: What component compresses intake air before it passes through the intercooler?

options.text: The compressor, driven by the turbine
The waste gate valve
The alternate air valve
The ECU metering valve

explanation: AFM 7.9.8: intake air is compressed by the turbine-driven compressor, then cooled in the intercooler to increase density and power.

question: What controls the position of the waste gate valve in the turbocharger system?

options.text: A fixed mechanical spring with no active control
The ECU, based on a manifold pressure sensor behind the compressor
The pilot, via a dedicated waste-gate lever
The propeller governor

explanation: AFM 7.9.8: the ECU calculates the correct waste gate position from a manifold pressure sensor reading, preventing excessive manifold pressure at low density altitudes.

question: How is the fire detection system on each engine tested during the pre-flight inspection?

options.text: There is no pre-flight self-test; it is checked only during maintenance
By manually heating the overheat detector with a hand-held device
By pushing the test button next to the gear selector switch, checking for an aural alert and fire warning message for LH and RH
By momentarily setting ENGINE MASTER OFF then back ON

explanation: AFM 7.9.9 (and 4A.6.1) describe testing the fire detection system with the test button beside the gear selector, confirming an aural alert and PFD fire warning for each engine.

question: Each engine's fire detection consists of what kind of sensor?

options.text: A smoke detector in the engine cowling
A CO2 concentration sensor
A vibration sensor tuned to combustion knock
An overheat detector in the hot area of the engine

explanation: AFM 7.9.9 describes an overheat detector per engine that closes an electric circuit above 250 °C (480 °F), triggering the fire warning.

question: What indications for the LH and RH engines are shown on the G1000 MFD, and how are they arranged?

options.text: LH engine indications on the left side of the display, RH engine indications on the right
Both engines' data interleaved in a single combined column
RH engine on the left, LH engine on the right
Only the active (VOTER-selected) engine is shown at a time

explanation: AFM 7.9.4 states engine indications on the G1000 MFD are laid out with LH engine data on the left and RH engine data on the right, mirroring the airplane.
